name: Infineon Kulim 3 silicon carbide power fab

parties.name: Government of Malaysia
parties.note: The prime minister welcomed the 2023 expansion and attended the 2024 opening; no incentive amount is stated in the cited sources.

summary: A third front-end module at Infineon's Kulim site in Malaysia for silicon carbide power semiconductors, with gallium nitride epitaxy, on 200 mm wafers. Announced in February 2022 as a module of more than €2 billion, it was enlarged in August 2023 with a second construction phase of up to €5 billion. The first phase opened in August 2024 and Infineon reported a volume production ramp in fiscal 2025, but in November 2024 the company postponed the second phase and further cleanroom capacity because of weak demand.

location.note: Third module at Infineon's existing Kulim manufacturing site.

metrics.note: First phase; the opening release gives about €2 billion.
Second construction phase over five years; postponed in November 2024.
High-value jobs from the first phase.

milestones.note: Construction start planned for June 2022 at announcement.
At announcement Infineon expected the fab to be ready for equipment in summer 2024 and the first wafers in the second half of 2024.
Official opening of the first phase.
The 2025 annual report names the ramp-up of silicon carbide volume production in Kulim among the fiscal 2025 (October 2024 to September 2025) investment priorities.
Infineon said it would postpone further cleanroom capacity at Kulim, delaying the second phase.

sources.title: Infineon doubles down on wide bandgap by investing more than €2 billion in a new Kulim, Malaysia frontend fab to expand market leadership in power semiconductors
Infineon to build the world’s largest 200-millimeter SiC Power Fab in Kulim, Malaysia, leading to total revenue potential of about seven billion euros by the end of the decade
Infineon opens the world’s largest and most efficient SiC power semiconductor fab in Malaysia
